ideas.title: The Protocol War Nobody Is Winning: Why ACP vs. UCP Misses the Most Important Commerce Moment of All
ideas.insider_angle: Google's UCP and OpenAI's ACP define the agent-to-merchant handshake — but both assume the commerce journey begins when a user opens a chat interface, search box, or voice query. Neither protocol has a surface type for 'lockscreen card.' Glance's Zapps are zero-install transactional surfaces operating at device wake, before any agent session is invoked — making Glance the D0 commerce node that feeds into whichever protocol wins downstream. McKinsey estimates AI agents could redirect $3–5T in global retail spend by 2030; Glance controls the trigger point that initiates the entire agentic payment chain.
ideas.calendar_hook: ACP vs. UCP protocol war intensifying week of June 16; CommerceNext Growth Show June 23–24 (heavy agentic AI agenda)
ideas.opening_hook: Two protocols are racing to become the backbone of AI commerce — one backed by OpenAI and Stripe, one by Google and Amazon — and the entire industry is debating which will win, while missing the one moment neither protocol even has a spec for.
ideas.why_now: The ACP/UCP protocol war is at peak coverage intensity this week across agentcommerce.substack, robonomics, and commercetools; 'best agentic checkout platforms comparison 2026' is a P1 high-volume query currently owned by Search Engine Journal and Opascope but with a clear Glance whitespace angle none of them cover, and CommerceNext in one week will amplify the protocol conversation.
